Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition.
2. Create a new world with Superflat settings.
3. In the "Layers" section of the Superflat world generator, set the layer to `minecraft:air;127;decoration`.
4. Leave all other settings as default and do not add any biomes or layers.
5. Click the "Done" button to generate the world.
6. Observe that the game crashes immediately after clicking "Done".
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3
Observed Behavior: When creating a superflat world with only air blocks in Minecraft version 1.16.2, clicking the "Done" button after setting up the world configuration causes the game to crash. The specific configuration used is `1 minecraft:air;127;decoration`, which results in an error message indicating that a required biome resource key is missing. This issue can be reproduced by attempting to create such a superflat world and observing the subsequent crash upon finalizing the setup. The associated crash report, titled "crash-2020-08-20_16.04.11-client.txt," provides detailed information about the error, including the stack trace that points to the missing biome resource key as the root cause of the crash. Developers can use this information to diagnose and fix the issue, ensuring that the game does not crash when attempting to create a superflat world with only air blocks.
Expected Behavior: When creating a superflat world with only air blocks, the game should not crash upon clicking the "Done" button. Instead, the world generation process should complete successfully, resulting in a flat world composed entirely of air without any other blocks or biomes. The game should remain stable and allow normal gameplay within this unique world configuration.
